Immediate post-test only; no delayed retention wave and no CIs reported. Also circulated as CRC TRR 190 DP 557; working paper, not yet peer-reviewed.
estimation_method: Covariate-adjusted OLS (Table 1, Col. 2); controls: Test 1 baseline score, Bachelor, field-of-study/semester/session FE; heteroskedasticity-robust SE

study_label: Gan et al., orthopedics
outcome: Post-intervention 214-item orthopedics examination (unassisted post-test): number of MCQs answered correctly (max 214)
treatment: ChatGPT-4 self-study: 1-week orthopedics review using only ChatGPT-4.0 (other search engines and message boards not allowed)
control: Internet/forums self-study: 1-week orthopedics review using search engines and message boards; no OpenAI-connected software allowed
notes: 129 assessed for eligibility; 4 excluded before randomization (2 not meeting criteria, 2 declining); 125 randomized (60 ChatGPT, 65 control; CONSORT Figure 1). 15 withdrew after randomization (7 initial study, 8 follow-up); 110 analyzed complete-case (54 ChatGPT, 56 control). No ITT analysis. Primary exam: ChatGPT 141.20 (SD 26.68) vs control 130.80 (SD 25.56); mean difference 10.40 with reported SE 4.98 (labeled 'SD' in the paper), P=.04; Cohen's d=0.398 (SE 0.193) back-calculated from per-arm means/SDs (pooled SD 26.12). PAPER TYPO: the Results body misprints the ChatGPT exam mean as 138.46 (SD 26.97); the abstract value 141.20 (SD 26.68) is the correct one (it reproduces the 10.40 difference and the 4.98 SE). Sub-scores favored ChatGPT on A1 (P=.01), A2 (P=.047), and A3/A4 (P=.002); case-analysis items non-significantly lower for ChatGPT (diff -1.04, P=.16). Unassisted post-test by design (formal examination separate from the learning-phase exercises), though the paper never states the exam was proctored/closed-book or that AI was barred during testing.
estimation_method: Independent-samples 2-tailed t test on per-arm exam means (SPSS 26); Cohen's d=0.398 (SE 0.193) back-calculated from means/SDs (pooled SD 26.12); reported raw difference 10.40 with SE 4.98 (matches sqrt(26.68^2/54+25.56^2/56)=4.985), t=2.09, P=.04.

outcome: Downstream end-of-semester surgery final examination score (secondary long-term outcome)
treatment: ChatGPT-4 self-study: 1-week orthopedics review using only ChatGPT-4.0 (other search engines and message boards not allowed)
control: Internet/forums self-study: 1-week orthopedics review using search engines and message boards; no OpenAI-connected software allowed
notes: Secondary downstream end-of-semester final exams (same arms; 54 ChatGPT, 56 control), measured June 2023 with no additional intervention in the interim; 2 control students reported some LLM use, all ChatGPT-arm students used LLMs. Surgery significant: ChatGPT 76.54 (SD 9.79) vs control 72.54 (SD 8.11); diff 4.00 (SE 1.72), P=.02. OB/GYN also significant: 75.98 (SD 8.94) vs 72.54 (SD 8.66); diff 3.45 (SE 1.68), P=.04. Non-significant: internal medicine (diff 0.23, SE 1.58, P=.88); pediatrics (diff -1.58, SE 1.79, P=.38, ChatGPT lower); infectious diseases (diff 1.60, SE 1.75, P=.36). Total final-exam score diff 7.71 (SE 7.53), P=.31 (n.s.). Cohen's d=0.446 (SE 0.193) for the surgery exam back-calculated from per-arm means/SDs (76.54 (SD 9.79, n=54) vs 72.54 (SD 8.11, n=56); pooled SD 8.97); consistent with the reported diff 4.00 / SE 1.72 (t=2.33, P=.02). Added in the 2026-07 RA verification round. Final-exam scale not stated (scores ~72-77). SE values are the between-group difference SEs (paper labels them 'SD').
coding_notes: secondary/downstream outcome; per-protocol (complete-case); d back-calculated from means/SDs
estimation_method: Independent-samples 2-tailed t test on per-arm surgery final-exam means (SPSS 26); reported raw mean difference 4.00 with SE 1.72 (labeled 'SD'), P=.02; no SD-scale effect computed (per-arm SDs available: 9.79 vs 8.11).

study_label: Hou et al., guided AI
outcome: Unassisted post-test total score (max 27): 9 MCQ (auto-scored) + 18 open-ended (human-scored by two blind raters, ICC=0.91), administered after the AI-assisted review phase
treatment: Prompted (guided) AI review: RAG assistant use guided by a five-step Generative-Learning-Theory framework (Clarify, Organize, Integrate, Differentiate, Correct)
control: Continued slide/PowerPoint review of the same materials, independently, with no AI access
notes: Total post-test (max 27 = 9 MCQ auto-scored + 18 open-ended human-scored). Guided/prompted AI (5-step GLT framework) vs slide-only control: 18.86 vs 15.35 (+3.51 points), d=0.864. Effect concentrated in open-ended reasoning (12.41 vs 9.68 on max 18, d~1.06; omnibus 3-group F=7.32, p=0.0011); no MCQ effect (6.45 vs 5.67, F=2.38, p=0.099, ns). SE(d)=0.266 back-calculated from Table 3 means/SDs/Ns; paper reports only omnibus one-way ANOVA (total F=6.82, p=0.0017), not pairwise tests. Contrast n=62 (29 prompted + 33 control); n_total=95 is the full analytic sample across all three arms. AI used only during the review phase; the post-test itself is unassisted. Post-test-only design (no pre-test covariate).
coding_notes: back-calculated SEs; omnibus F reported, pairwise d derived; 20% excluded for incomplete data
estimation_method: One-way three-group ANOVA on the total post-test (omnibus F=6.82, p=0.0017); pairwise Cohen's d for the prompted arm vs the slide-only control back-calculated from Table 3 means/SDs/Ns, SE(d) from the standard large-sample formula sqrt((n1+n2)/(n1*n2) + d^2/(2(n1+n2))). Complete-case analysis (95 of 119 retained; 24 dropped for incomplete data).

study_label: Hou et al., unguided AI
outcome: Unassisted post-test total score (max 27): 9 MCQ (auto-scored) + 18 open-ended (human-scored by two blind raters, ICC=0.91), administered after the AI-assisted review phase
treatment: Unprompted (free) AI review: students query the RAG assistant freely, with no structured prompts
control: Continued slide/PowerPoint review of the same materials, independently, with no AI access
notes: Total post-test (max 27 = 9 MCQ + 18 open-ended). Unprompted/free AI (free-form querying of the RAG assistant, no structured prompts) vs slide-only control: 15.73 vs 15.35 (+0.38 points), d=0.093 -- essentially no effect. Open-ended 10.45 vs 9.68 (d~0.27); MCQ 5.27 vs 5.67 (d~-0.19). SE(d)=0.246 back-calculated from Table 3 means/SDs/Ns; paper reports only omnibus one-way ANOVA (total F=6.82, p=0.0017), not pairwise tests. Contrast n=66 (33 unprompted + 33 control); n_total=95 is the full analytic sample across all three arms. AI used only during the review phase; the post-test itself is unassisted. Free AI use was no better than slide-only review.
coding_notes: back-calculated SEs; omnibus F reported, pairwise d derived; 20% excluded for incomplete data
estimation_method: One-way three-group ANOVA on the total post-test (omnibus F=6.82, p=0.0017); pairwise Cohen's d for the unprompted arm vs the slide-only control back-calculated from Table 3 means/SDs/Ns, SE(d) from the standard large-sample formula sqrt((n1+n2)/(n1*n2) + d^2/(2(n1+n2))). Complete-case analysis (95 of 119 retained; 24 dropped for incomplete data).

study_label: Huang et al., dental skills
outcome: Desktop-VR operative skill test (0-100, auto-scored by the VR system, taken unassisted within 15 min after 1-week training)
treatment: ChatGPT-3.5 as a supplementary instructor added to instructional videos (free version; used during a 1-week skill-acquisition period to resolve doubts, verify procedures, and give extra guidance)
notes: ChatGPT-3.5 (free version) added to instructional videos vs identical videos only (blank control); ChatGPT is the sole additive difference. Raw operative-test scores 73.12 (SD 10.06) vs 65.54 (SD 12.48) on a 0-100 auto-scored desktop-VR task; mean diff 7.58 points, Welch t(176.24)=4.569, P<.001. N=187 analyzed (192 recruited, 5 excluded at eye-tracking calibration; 94 ChatGPT vs 93 control). Baseline theoretical-knowledge test balanced (41.24 vs 42.03, P=.52). No AI during the test (design inference; the paper does not explicitly state ChatGPT was blocked at test). Cohen's d=0.669, SE=0.150, 95% CI ~0.38-0.96 back-calculated from per-arm means/SDs/n; no author-reported standardized effect. Effect concentrated among low-spatial-ability students (70.20 vs 55.41, P<.001) and absent among high-spatial-ability students (76.58 vs 73.89, P=.22). Secondary outcomes favored ChatGPT: self-efficacy P=.04, learning motivation P=.02, cognitive load via pupil-diameter change 0.137 vs 0.312 P<.001.
estimation_method: Independent-samples Welch t test on post-test desktop-VR operative scores, t(176.24)=4.569, P<.001 (normality checked via Shapiro-Wilk); complete-case on the 187 students who passed eye-tracking calibration. Cohen's d and its SE (0.150) back-calculated from reported per-arm means, SDs, and n; no author-reported standardized effect.

control: Literature-research group searched the internet and scientific literature (the module's traditional method) to complete the same assignment
notes: 77 students randomized (39 ChatGPT, 38 literature); 70 sat the unannounced exam (39 ChatGPT, 31 literature; 7 absent). Cohen's d and SE back-calculated from means/SDs/n (paper reports no CI or standardized effect). Modest instrument (10 MCQs); grades ranged 5-10.
coding_notes: d back-calculated from means/SDs; 10-item multiple-choice exam
estimation_method: Mann-Whitney U test on exam grades (nonparametric, SPSS v25); standardized effect (Cohen's d) and SE back-calculated from group means, SDs, and n. Complete-case: 70 of 77 randomized students sat the exam.

study_label: LearnLM, Sierra Leone
outcome: IRT-scaled endline math assessment (Oxford MeasurEd), unassisted; intent-to-treat
treatment: Gemini "Guided Learning" integrated by teachers into half of weekly math lessons (~12h over 8 weeks, students in pairs)
notes: Table C.4 col 2 (baseline-adjusted ANCOVA); the paper's headline intent-to-treat estimate, in SD units of the IRT-scaled endline math score. n_total=1,763 is the enrolled sample; the estimate is analyzed on the balanced panel (present at both baseline and endline), N=1,423 (711 control, 712 treatment); baseline N=1,547, endline N=1,637. 95% CI [0.027, 0.488], p=0.029. Unadjusted ITT = +0.216 SD (SE 0.137, not significant); fully adjusted (adds gender, age) = +0.259 SD (95% CI [0.025, 0.494], p=0.031). Authors benchmark 0.258 SD as roughly 1.2-1.7 years of extra learning in LMICs and a 50th-to-60th percentile move. Gemini 2.5 Pro for first six weeks, 3.0 Pro for final three weeks. Uptake: 69.0% of the 871 treatment students reached the requested 12h; treatment classrooms averaged ~15h. Field monitors (one per school, 12 total) documented no spillover beyond two isolated incidents, and any spillover would attenuate the estimate. Heterogeneity: effect rises +0.195 SD per baseline-math SD (p=0.002), favoring higher-baseline students.
estimation_method: OLS with baseline math+reading scores, block FE; SE clustered at classroom (48 clusters)
